scores.evidence: Retrieved and user text go in delimited data sections, never in the system instructions.
scores.rationale: Mechanisms are accurate (alias swap, hybrid search, allow-list indexing), but the plan leans on delimiting as injection defense and does not say it is only partial. Deletion handling is also unstated.

scores.evidence: Assumed no: anonymous visitors, public docs only, no account data, no actions, English only.
scores.rationale: It covers the core RAG needs with explicit scope and deferrals, but it does not specify the index update window or how deletions are handled.

scores.evidence: Allow-list indexing: only articles with an explicit public flag. No per-user ACL because there is no user data.
scores.rationale: The design is consistent, with clear responsibilities and uniform use of the alias and flag. There are minor loose ends, such as the 'iteration caps' wording for a no-tools bot and Redis session state against the 'no persistent PII' claim.

scores.evidence: 0 violations ... across ≥ 200 cases; ... hit@5 ≥ 90% ... 0 canary docs retrieved; ... ≥ 95% of sampled answers fully supported
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, with a canary doc, injection suite, SME review and a V0 spike early. Thresholds are labeled as assumptions, and the eval runs in CI and in canary. Post-launch regression monitoring is lighter.

scores.evidence: Missing inputs (none changes the phase order, but each changes a threshold or scope)
scores.rationale: Figures are labeled ASSUMPTION or UNKNOWN with owners and dates, and the plan says what re-plans if an assumption is wrong.

scores.evidence: a failed sync leaves the previous index serving.
scores.rationale: It covers injection, leaks, runaway cost, vendor outage, bad sync and wrong high-risk answers with concrete handling. Staleness and deletion detection, and partial failures, are thinner.

scores.evidence: Feature flag off (kill switch), redeploy the previous image, or swap the index alias back.
scores.rationale: It covers rollback, OTel tracing, alerts, SLO and on-call ownership sized to the existing team. Incident response and review cadence are only lightly specified.

scores.evidence: AI inference cost, per session | ≤ 20k tokens, ≤ 6 model calls
scores.rationale: Caps and controls are concrete, but there is no cost estimate per conversation, cost per resolution is UNKNOWN, and build and people costs are not covered.

scores.evidence: Build vs buy | R2: a vendor switch means weeks of re-integration and re-eval
scores.rationale: Each decision carries a reversibility class, a validation and a revisit trigger. The plan isolates vendor coupling behind a provider interface, pins the embedding model and versions the index.

scores.evidence: Orchestration | Not needed: a single retrieve-then-answer call
scores.rationale: It is a minimal design with multi-agent, routing and fine-tuning explicitly deferred. The process tables are slightly heavy but justified.

scores.evidence: Exit check (V0): A real question succeeds with one trace across every tier. A deploy and a rollback succeed
scores.rationale: Walking-skeleton-first ordering is justified by dependencies, with checkable exit checks per phase and explicit fail actions.

checklist.evidence: Re-index on doc publish (webhook plus nightly full sync).
Chunking: by article heading, with hybrid BM25 plus embedding search.
≥ 150 real queries sampled from past tickets and search logs.
answer only from retrieved passages, always cite, and abstain or hand off when retrieval confidence is low
a "talk to a person" path that creates a ticket with the transcript.
The chat service has no tools and no outbound calls.
Allow-list indexing: only articles with an explicit public flag.
Redact PII before logging and before the model call. Vendor on no-training, zero or minimal retention. Chat logs kept 30 days
Assumed no: anonymous visitors, public docs only, no account data, no actions
Add thumbs up/down, a "did this solve it?" prompt, and an unanswered-question report to the docs team.

traps.evidence: answer only from retrieved passages, always cite, and abstain or hand off
Allow-list indexing: only articles with an explicit public flag.
Run the retrieval eval in CI.
Not needed: a single retrieve-then-answer call

note: This is a strong, well-scoped and well-validated plan. Its gaps are the deletion and staleness window, the lack of a per-conversation cost estimate, and the escalation triggers and context handoff being only partly specified.
